steps.what: Read and critically assess current hacking trends and professional reports

tasks.design: Protect critical reading and understanding. Reports in {DOCS} support the tester's learning; a digest alone does not establish that a reported trend is credible or relevant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trend claims vary in quality and may repeat old findings under a new label.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change removes the need to assess the underlying evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing meaningful changes from publicity and uncertain attribution.
tasks.human_edge: The tester relates a report to actual security assumptions and evidence quality.
tasks.altitude: Maintaining informed professional judgement remains part of the week.

reach.learn: Explain the source and limits of the reported change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: professional knowledge of hacking trends requires critical reading rather than only collecting headlines.

assumptions: Boundary is professional trend learning, excluding a specific threat-technique investigation and any live testing.
No structured credible-trend flag is assumed; tester assesses source and meaning within s1's retained 100 hours.
Use existing professional feeds and references before new software; current collection runtime earns no saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new process or technology is proposed.
unknowns: Current source mix and learning priorities
research_questions: Which reported trends remain credible after examining their original evidence?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Critical learning keeps its time; no headline-collection baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate new penetration-testing tools and methods

steps.what: Study new penetration-testing tools and methods and their limitations
Evaluate tool behaviour and methods in an authorised isolated learning environment

tasks.design: Keep tool learning and method assessment with the tester using {DOCS} and an authorised {OTHER} security training lab. Existing automation features may be studied, but their execution runtime is not a saving in the tester's learning task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documentation alone cannot establish practical limitations or safe operating assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: An isolated lab supports direct evaluation without changing the learning responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising misleading output and limits that do not appear in simple demonstrations.
tasks.human_edge: The tester challenges tool claims through controlled observation.
tasks.altitude: Tool-selection judgement and practical learning remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish observed behaviour from advertised capability

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: learning a security tool requires examining its behaviour and limitations in a controlled environment.

assumptions: Boundary is professional tool and method learning, not a customer penetration test or production assessment.

Existing lab owner provides the authorised isolated environment and synthetic assets before s2. Tester selects questions in s1 and observes behaviour in s2's counted time; no model-produced safe-tool flag is presumed.
Use existing lab and documentation before adding software; current runtime is not new labour saved.
Zero upkeep because the proposal introduces no changed tool or learning process.
unknowns: Tools and methods relevant to current engagements
research_questions: Which limitations only become visible in controlled practical evaluation?

already_counted.description: Documentation study and controlled practical learning

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. All practical learning and assessment remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select reliable threat reports and the current technique catalogue for comparison
Extract reported tactics, techniques and procedures and compare existing coverage

loop.purpose: Draft reported technique observations and catalogue differences
loop.input: Tester-selected report extracts and a versioned existing technique catalogue
loop.output: One comparison table with source passages and explicit uncertainty for possible new observations
loop.check: Tester checks each observation against original evidence, distinguishes reported fact from attribution or speculation and verifies whether the difference is genuinely absent from the catalogue
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported claims, ambiguous provenance or unavailable catalogue context return to manual comparison; no external search or tool execution
loop.why_not_simpler: Native catalogue search comes first; unfamiliar narrative reports may describe the same technique in different words, requiring semantic comparison

steps.what: Determine whether the reported technique is new and document evidence limits

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} catalogue search first, then a bounded comparison draft for selected narrative reports. The tester verifies the source claims and decides what is genuinely new; no actor attribution or live testing is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports describe similar behaviour in different language and mix observation with speculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound comparison can supply a first table for expert checking.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a new technique from a new name or an unsupported claim.
tasks.human_edge: The tester weighs evidence quality and recognises uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less initial comparison writing while novelty and relevance judgements remain human.

reach.learn: Trace the claim to its original evidence and uncertainty

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a model can draft semantic comparisons of selected reports, but novelty and attribution require source checking and expert judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is documentary identification and comparison, excluding live threat hunting, actor profiling and execution of test techniques.

Tester captures source identity, publication date, selected passages, catalogue version and investigation scope in s1's 25 hours. Original publishers produce the reports as unchanged external work; missing provenance or catalogue entries require manual review rather than an inferred new-technique flag.
Try native catalogue search before a model; existing feed runtime is not labour saved.
No confidential engagement material or credentials enter drafting without locally approved access.
research_questions: Do draft differences survive expert source checking and reduce comparison effort after rejected claims?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=88.75, gross=11.25 and net=6.25 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes useful source-grounded comparison drafts; novelty judgement retains all its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Audit network and security systems against criteria

steps.what: Confirm audit authority, target scope and established evidence criteria
Collect specified read-only configuration and security evidence from authorised systems
Compare explicit configuration values with the established audit criteria
Assess evidence, exceptions and the significance of audit discrepancies
Report audit conclusions and evidence limitations

tasks.design: Configure {OTHER} native read-only exports and fixed comparisons for the approved audit criteria. The tester assesses discrepancies and writes the conclusions in {DOCS}; missing evidence remains unassessed rather than automatically passing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated evidence retrieval and exact-value comparisons can consume audit effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and configured comparison rules can produce traceable evidence tables.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence freshness, compensating controls and the significance of a discrepancy.
tasks.human_edge: The tester decides what the evidence actually establishes in the audited context.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated evidence manipulation while scope, findings and audit conclusions remain accountable human work.

reach.learn: Separate raw comparison results from assessed risk

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: read-only configuration exports and explicit comparators can support audits without determining overall compliance or risk.

assumptions: Boundary is an authorised evidence-based audit; active penetration testing, exploitation and remediation are excluded.

Tester captures target identifiers, authorised read-only source queries, audit window, criterion IDs and versions, exact fields, comparators and expected values in s1's 20 hours. Existing system owners produce configuration and access records; missing exports or unsupported schema stop collection for manual evidence handling. No automatically inferred compliant flag is assumed.
Test native audit exports before custom code; the 45% share requires observed manual collection and exact comparisons, not existing scanner or query runtime.
Only exact-value criteria are compared automatically; contextual or documentary criteria remain in s4 with positive time.
unknowns: Available native exports and audit authority
Share of criteria requiring contextual assessment
research_questions: Does a read-only trial reproduce manual evidence tables while clearly marking every unassessed criterion?

already_counted.description: Authority, scope and exact criterion capture

incremental.description: Criteria mapping upkeep and manual evidence exceptions
Additional periodic export-access and schema checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact evidence specification version, authorised target set, read-only queries, data fields and audit window approved in s1; any expansion voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55, gross=45 and net=36 after nine focal upkeep hours. Range assumes partly manual read-only evidence collection and exact comparisons; contextual assessment and conclusions retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repetitive audit evidence handling and first comparison drafts while retaining source scepticism, learning and audit judgement.
reach: Explain evidence-backed control discrepancies to security engineers
role.ambitious_version: A penetration tester who spends more attention on what evidence means and less on repeated evidence manipulation, within explicit authorised scope.
